terms.gloss: a doer, a manager who acts for another; here, an AI agent
evidence: Tac. Ann. 2.30: āctor pūblicus, the manager of public property (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Sest. 28 (by chapter):Catō dux, auctor, āctor rērum illārum fuit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classically one who does a thing, and later an agent or steward who manages property for its owner (Lewis & Short): both are what an AI agent is, a program that acts on its own for someone. The use is modern, and ours. Vicipaedia is reported to call an intelligent agent āctor intellegēns (MatMedia); we could not open the article. For an agent who is a person see agent, someone who acts for another; for a part on the stage, actor.

phrases.latin: Āctor epistulās perlēgit et ad singulās respondit.
phrases.english: The agent read through the emails and answered each one.

sources: Lewis & Short: actor
MatMedia, “L’Intelligenza Artificiale in lingua latina!”
